record.paper_title: Separability of Topological Groups: A Survey with Open Problems
record.original_question: Does every infinite-dimensional Banach space have a quotient Banach space that is both separable and infinite-dimensional?

evidence.quote: Does every infinite-dimensional Banach space have a quotient Banach space which is separable and infinite-dimensional?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
A Banach space is a complete normed vector space over the real or complex numbers. Given a Banach space $X$ and a closed linear subspace $Y \subseteq X$, the quotient $X/Y$ equipped with the norm $\|x+Y\| = \inf_{y\in Y}\|x-y\|$ is again a Banach space, called a quotient Banach space of $X$. A Banach space is separable if it contains a countable dense subset.

Determine whether the following statement is true: every infinite-dimensional Banach space $X$ admits a closed subspace $Y$ such that the quotient Banach space $X/Y$ is both infinite-dimensional and separable.
artifact.status_search_result: The question is the classical Banach–Mazur separable quotient problem, posed by Mazur in 1932. It remains open in general. Affirmative answers are known for many classes of Banach spaces, including reflexive spaces, weakly compactly generated spaces, dual spaces, and more recently "dual-like" Banach spaces, but the general case is still unresolved.

status_evidence.title: Observations on the Separable Quotient Problem for Banach Spaces
status_evidence.snippet: The longstanding Banach–Mazur separable quotient problem asks whether every infinite-dimensional Banach space has a quotient that is both infinite-dimensional and separable.
status_evidence.claim: The problem remains open in general, with affirmative answers in special cases (reflexive, WCG, dual spaces).

status_evidence.title: Revisiting Mazur separable quotient problem (1932)
status_evidence.snippet: The centenary of the still open problem of the existence of a separable quotient of infinite dimension in a Banach space will be in 2032.
status_evidence.claim: The problem is still open as of recent surveys.

status_evidence.title: On the separable quotient problem for Banach spaces
status_evidence.snippet: The Banach–Mazur separable quotient problem has remained unsolved for 85 years.
